title: Test Drive
build: Decibel and Eagle Soft Incorporated side A, Eagle Soft Incorporated side B

Low byte of the C64 bitmap offset for each raster row. Entries use 320 times the character row plus the row within its eight-line band.
Low byte of the relative bitmap address starting at scanline 60. The low byte wraps every four character rows.
The low byte of the relative bitmap address for pixel rows 124–187. The row formula is 320 times the character row plus the scanline within the cell. This slice continues the table at $0400.
The low byte of the relative bitmap address for pixel rows 188–251. The row formula is 320 times the character row plus the scanline within the cell. This slice continues the table at $0400.
The low byte of the relative bitmap address for pixel rows 252–255. The row formula is 320 times the character row plus the scanline within the cell. This slice continues the table at $0400.
High byte companion to the table at $0400. The renderer adds the chosen bitmap bank to this relative offset.

Continuation of the high-byte bitmap address table from scanline 60, ending just before scanline 124.
The high byte of the relative bitmap address for pixel rows 124–187. The row formula is 320 times the character row plus the scanline within the cell. This slice continues the table at $0500.
The high byte of the relative bitmap address for pixel rows 188–251. The row formula is 320 times the character row plus the scanline within the cell. This slice continues the table at $0500.
The high byte of the relative bitmap address for pixel rows 252–255. The row formula is 320 times the character row plus the scanline within the cell. This slice continues the table at $0500.

Forty low bytes of seven times the destination column.

Resident jump table entry to $0C4F. This looks up the two-byte module ID in X and Y and arranges for the module to be present in memory.

Resident jump table entry to $1244, using the two-byte module ID in X and Y.
Resident entry for finding an already loaded descriptor by its ID.

Zero-filled space in the DM load after the main resident jump table. The driving overlay uses part of it at $0836–$0844 for the five FX service jumps.

Zero-filled end of the page before the module directory at $0900.

Crosses the end of TD’s descriptor into UJ and the following loaded modules. Each entry records the payload size and address independently.
Tail of the first sampled-audio descriptor, the second sample descriptor and the two color assets immediately preceding the entry at $0997.

High address byte of the matched module’s payload.

High address byte of the matched directory record.

Template for the initial populated records in the resident directory. Setup copies through the limit at $09FB before clearing the remaining slots.
Most recently stored drive reply, with one byte of space before the active command field.

Return the most recently stored drive reply in A.
Save the transfer command, send it with the physical track and sector, then handle read or write data. For a write, send 256 source bytes and their rolling XOR before reading the drive reply.
Shift incoming serial bits from CIA2 port A into $FF. The handshaking paths rotate a one or a zero and return when the marker shifts out.
Output the byte over the CIA2 serial handshaking lines, with one bit handled per iteration.
Send the requested disk side command through the resident transfer path.
Rolling XOR checksum for the active serial sector transfer.
Save the caller's module pointer and requested ID, search resident records through $131E, and consult the disk directory for a module missing from memory.
Read the two-byte payload length from the private directory, allocate a resident destination, then transfer the initial partial sector, whole sectors and final partial sector.
Reserve a directory record, copy its flags, ID and length from the disk descriptor, then store the new allocation's address. Extend the directory if $09FC indicates that another block is required.

Copy the starting track and sector into the transfer descriptor and use the disk item's byte offset to decide whether to read a partial sector. Limit the first copy to the payload length when it fits within the sector.
Patched low address of the partial-sector read buffer.
Patched high address of the partial-sector read. Copy the remaining bytes from the first sector before advancing the sector counter.
Subtract the bytes already copied, advance the logical track and sector with 16 sectors per track, and transfer any whole sectors directly into the remaining payload area.
Read a trailing sector when the low byte of the remaining payload length is nonzero. Patch the source operand from the sector transfer descriptor and copy only that many bytes.
Low operand byte of the indexed sector buffer read used for the final partial transfer.
High operand byte of the sector buffer read at $0E6F. Copy X remaining bytes to the payload and return its allocation address.
Preserve the result in $0A4A while clearing the lookup's busy flag and restoring the requested ID and previous $06 pointer.

Read a two-byte allocation size from the caller's stack and reject an ID already in the resident directory. Reserve payload storage and fill the new descriptor with flags $02, the requested ID, its length and its address. Return the address in $04 on success.
If bit 7 of $1C29 is set, print the allocation error and requested ID. Return with carry set.
Search cache pages beginning at $0900 for a free record position, using the ordering of the stored address fields.
Save the pending transfer's pointers and length, request $F9 bytes through the allocator, and link the resulting directory block.
Examine the module allocation records to find space for the length at $09F9-$09FA. The branch at $1119 switches to the alternate search starting at $11C6.
Search the loaded module directory from $0900 for the ID in X and Y, remove its record, and restore X and Y before returning.
High address byte of the indexed deletion-compaction load. The following loop copies seven-byte records toward the freed slot.
Low byte of the source page patched for final record compaction.
High byte of the compaction copy source. Finish moving entries up to offset $F9, then patch both stores with the final vacancy address.
Low operand byte of the seven-byte store into the final slot in the preceding page.
High operand byte of the cross-page compaction store. Copy the next page’s first record back into the slot and continue from that page.
Low operand byte shared with the cross-page compaction path. The zeroing loop erases the final slot when there is no next page.
High operand byte of the clearing store. If the remaining linked page is now empty, sever its link from the preceding page and release the page record.
Follow the directory list starting at $0900 and compare the packed two-byte IDs against X and Y. When found, copy the seven-byte descriptor to $0A01 and return its payload pointer in $04.
Return immediately from the service jump at $080C.
Save A, X and Y, then print the high and low nibbles of A using the hexadecimal character table at $13C3. Restore the original registers.
Map the nibble in A through the hexadecimal glyph table, then jump to the resident character printer.
PETSCII digits zero through nine followed by A through F, used by $13BC.
Saved X argument for the resident text output wrapper.
Original output character saved while updating the quoted-text flag.
Saved Y argument restored when the character wrapper returns.
Quoted-text flag. Toggle on a double quote and clear on carriage return.

Save A, X and Y for character output. In unquoted state, byte $07 calls module $42/$21 with the bitmap pointer at $04 preserved. A double quote toggles the quote state, and carriage return clears it. Non-bell output goes through $16D2. Restore A, X and Y on return.
Operand byte of the CPY immediate at $1441. The flag lookup at $1515 uses this as an indexed base, addressing later bytes for commands $D0 and $D1.
Select the VIC banking, bitmap and screen mode registers from the display mode in Y. Preserve the unrelated bits in VIC control and CIA2 port A.

Select the background color and screen fill byte. Disk configuration 3 selects the second six-entry group. Unless the display flag is negative, fill the chosen screen page and the four color RAM pages.
First screen destination page patched from the display mode.
Second screen destination page, one above the first.
Third screen destination page for the current mode.
Fourth screen destination page. Complete the 256-iteration screen fill, then fill all four color RAM pages with one.
Saved Y value used when the display service repeats the prior mode.
Saved display service X value for mode replay.
Saved display service A argument, also used as the mode for the screen-only fill command.
VIC control 1 bits to OR into the masked register value for each display mode.
CIA2 low bank-select bits indexed by display mode.
VIC memory pointer values indexed by display mode.
VIC control 2 multicolor bit indexed by display mode.
Screen fill bytes for the bank and display configuration selected by the mode.
Starting high page for the four-page screen fill. A zero skips the screen-matrix write.
VIC background color selected by display mode and disk configuration.

Pending character byte returned ahead of another GETIN call.
Saved processor port for the banked call to GETIN.
Toggle the $40 bit in the input-service flags. The alternate entry uses a BIT skip to share the toggle.
Resident service flags including the bit toggled by the $F3 input command.
Consume a queued character when present. Otherwise bank the KERNAL in for GETIN and restore the processor port. Translate the left-arrow code $5F to $1B.
Tail call to KERNAL GETIN while the ROM and I/O are mapped in.
Nonzero when the expansion-register probe succeeds.
Probe the RAM expansion register at $DF05 by writing and checking $FF and zero. On success set the presence flag and clear the sector bitmap.
Clear the second 88-byte bitmap beginning at $1C8A.
Enter the cache transfer path with expansion command $91 via a BIT skip.

Begin the sector transfer with command $90. The shared path below checks the expansion flag at $1596, chooses a bitmap byte based on track and disk side, and selects the sector bit with $1C2A. A command $90 marks a cached sector; the alternate command requires the bit already set. Carry is set if the expansion is disabled or the required sector is absent.
Opcode of the indexed staging write in the banked expansion transfer.
Low address operand patched from the allocated staging page pointer.

High byte of the store at $163D. When the sector buffer starts at or above $CF00, the $90 path banks out I/O, stages 256 bytes through the alternate address at $0A3E, then restores the processor port. The shared transfer at $1669 sends the command and length to the expansion registers.
Beginning of the source read in the expansion-to-main-memory copy loop.
Low source operand selected from the alternate transfer address.
High source operand of the staging read. Copy a full page after a cached read, restore banking and return with carry clear.
Nonzero when a cached read uses the staging page before copying to the requested banked destination.
Write the C64 address supplied in X and Y to the expansion transfer address registers.
Write the transfer length in X and Y, then issue the command in A to the expansion unit.
Encode the logical track in expansion memory address bits. Subtract three, add $2C for the other side, multiply by sixteen and merge the sector number.
Immediate logical sector patched from X before building the expansion address.
Save the caller’s A, X and Y into the return immediates. Temporarily enable the KERNAL and I/O, print the byte, then restore mapping and registers.
Immediate return A saved before the KERNAL output call.
Immediate return Y patched at $16D2.
Immediate return X patched at $16D5.
Tail call to KERNAL CHROUT.
Save A, X, Y and the port at $01. Enable I/O, build a return frame for $172E, call $1DE0 with the original frame's stack index and dispatch through the IRQ vector at $0314.
Save A and the port at $01, enable I/O and install a return frame for $1729 before dispatch through the NMI vector at $0318.
Restore the processor port and A from the NMI wrapper's stack, then return to the interrupted program.
Restore the processor port and Y, X and A from the IRQ wrapper's stack, then return to the interrupted program.

Clear the page at $1F00, configure the display and interrupt vectors, copy the initial directory from $0AA0 to $0900 and zero the unused directory slots. Allocate a 256-byte sector buffer and store its address in the transfer descriptor at $0A3E.
Branch operand before the resident startup display request. A nonzero boot flag sends display command $D2.
Set the indirect directory pointer $04–$05 to $0900.
Interleaved physical track and sector pairs for logical tracks starting at $24. The sector routine at $19AD uses twice the combined logical track and sector index.
The second byte of each track and sector pair. The transfer uses the same even index for the track at $1829 and the sector at $182A.
Processor mapping with I/O visible during disk signalling.
Alternate processor mapping used for the payload buffer access.

Copy the requested transfer descriptor into $0A0E and following bytes. Use logical sectors 0 through 15, translating higher logical tracks through $1829 before handing a physical position to the serial transfer.
Issue the final sector request using the command byte at $0A12 minus one. Save the result and return the carry from comparing it with two.
Disk lookup countdown tested before another catalogue scan.
Physical track byte sent after the drive command.
Physical sector byte sent after the track.
Save A, X and Y, load the requested module, adjust its entry word for the allocated address, and relocate references inside the module before invoking the entry.
Reload the calling registers saved at $0A17–$0A19 and jump indirectly through the relocated address at $0A52.

Patched continuation address high byte.

Preserve registers and the current module pointer. If the resident flag permits and MG resolves, invoke MG with the saved argument and then restore the caller’s state.
Saved argument read back after the MG service call.
Set the high bit of A by addition, call the MG wrapper and restore the original A and processor status.
Send the byte and then $28 over the parallel port. On timeout clear the debug enable bit and set the border to color one.
Send the two-byte trailer $29 and $0D over the parallel port. Either send can branch to the timeout handler.
Bank in I/O, send the byte through the parallel handshake with IRQs masked, then restore the processor port.
Parallel output flags. The high bit enables diagnostic calls, and the toggle path at $1528 flips bit zero.
One set bit per sector position within a sector-cache bitmap byte.
Bitmap of sectors marked present in the RAM expansion cache. Each track takes two bytes and side B adds an $58-byte displacement.
Upper portion of the first 88-byte sector-cache bitmap, extending through $1C89.
Second 88-byte bitmap used by the expansion cache paths and cleared by $15CE.
Final 24 bytes of the second bitmap, through the last index $57 of the clear routine.
Prepare the parallel handshake: make port B input, set bit two of port A as output, raise it, and clear pending CIA2 state before enabling IRQs.
Set CIA2 port B as output and write the requested byte. Pulse a line on port A, wait for the CIA2 handshake or the CIA1 timer, and return carry set on timeout.
Check CIA2's flag. If set, read the input byte from port B and pulse port A before returning the byte with carry set. Otherwise return carry clear.
Add A to the indirect write pointer at $04-$05.
Read bytes from CHRIN into $0200 until carriage return and restore the previous processor port.
Multiply the word in $33-$34 by the bit stream in $37, accumulating the result in $30-$31, then return its low byte in X and high byte in A.
Check the external command flag, look for the $AA handshake byte, echo it through the send routine, then handle the requested command.
KERNAL-side IRQ wrapper. Map in I/O, pass the adjusted stack position to $1DE0, restore the processor port and continue through $EA31.
The boot group starts with the descriptors for directory pages $00/$01 through $00/$04. The same sector contains the first part of the private item directory.
Further eight-byte item descriptors in the private disk directory. The length follows the two ID bytes, then come logical track, sector and the first payload byte offset.
More private item descriptors. The loader resolves the logical position from each record before reading the actual disk sectors.
Final private directory page. Trailing zero slots mark the end of the stored item records.
Relocated entry address $2504 followed by the TD body length $02F5.
Look up UJ and save the existing IRQ vector. Install the startup NMI and IRQ vectors stored in this module.
Load display, title, display-control, score and sound modules, then call PM to install the music player.
Call UJ for the $2A/$D4 and $2A/$CC archives and load the $C2/0 and $C2/1 resources between them.
Call TM, then walk the two-byte ID list at $27AA and release each entry through $0806 until the first zero ID byte.
Tag preceding the startup NMI address word.
Low byte of the startup NMI vector.
High byte of the startup NMI vector installed at $0319.
Save A and banking, disable CIA2 interrupt sources and read the interrupt register. Restore mapping and A before returning from NMI.
Tag preceding the startup IRQ address word.
Low byte of the startup IRQ vector.
High byte of the startup IRQ vector.
Map in I/O, acknowledge VIC IRQ status and increment the raster tick. Restore the processor port and continue to the KERNAL IRQ exit.
Call the resident display service with Y equal to $F2.
Put the resource ID and mode zero on the stack and invoke UJ. Then release the resource using the ID saved in the immediate operands at $27A3 and $27A5.
First immediate ID byte of the second title archive release call.
Second immediate ID byte of archive $2A/$CC before tail-calling the release service.
Zero byte separating the archive-release code from the title asset ID pairs.
Pairs of module and resource ID bytes used by the release loop at $25E1 after returning from TM. A zero first byte ends the list.
Second byte of the first title release ID followed by the rest of the two-byte IDs. The list includes the title sample pair, artwork children and finally song S1.
Final title release pairs, including $2D/$34, $2D/$35, the last bitmap and color assets, and S1, followed by the zero terminator.
IRQ vector saved from $0314 at TD entry and put back before its exit.
High byte of the IRQ vector saved on entering TD.
Relocated entry address $27FD followed by the UJ body length $01BF.
Save the return address and take the caller's resource mode and two-byte ID off the stack. Resolve the resource by ID and return the module lookup's error through the carry flag on failure.
Release work item $0C/$10 while preserving A and the caller's status, including the carry result.
Check directory flags against $37, copy the seven-byte header and require format $0C before allocating a temporary descriptor buffer.
Decode five-byte child descriptors into the temporary buffer, bounded by the descriptor count check at $289D. A zero flag starts the terminating descriptor.
Low operand byte of the current child-descriptor destination, advanced after each unpacked byte.
High operand of the patched descriptor store. On low-byte overflow increment this byte before processing the rest of the descriptor.
Read the four bytes after the terminal flag, then save the decoder byte and remaining repeat count for the first child.
Extract the child's expected length and ID, release a prior item with that ID and reserve storage for the replacement.
Patch the store target for the descriptor flags, then decode the child's declared number of bytes into its allocated address at $04.
Low operand of the patched flag store after reading the next descriptor.
High operand of the flag store. Restore the decoder repeat state and unpack the child bytes into the calculated output address.
Preserve the current repeat byte and count, move the descriptor pointer ahead five bytes, and advance the child index.

If X is nonzero, decrement it and return the repeat byte already in A. Otherwise decode a literal or one of four escape codes. The first escape reads a length from the stream and the others repeat their next byte three, four or five times.
Read the next packed byte through $0E and advance that 16-bit pointer.
Zero byte between the token reader and the unpacker’s seven-byte resource header buffer.
Seven bytes copied from the packed item by $284D. The first selects the format and offsets 3 through 6 hold the four escape codes.
Variable-length run escape byte for the resource decoder.
Escape byte that selects a three-byte run.
Escape byte that selects a four-byte run.
Escape byte that selects a five-byte run.
Two bytes from the caller's stack that the unpacker sends to the module lookup in X and Y.
Second ID byte saved for the requested packed resource.
Mode byte saved from the caller's stack alongside the resource ID.
Number of nonterminal descriptors decoded into the temporary buffer.
Index of the descriptor whose payload is being written.
Two-byte counter for the current child payload, tested before each decoded byte is written.
High byte of the remaining child payload count.
Saved output byte and repeat counter, restored between child allocations so a run can extend across a child boundary.
Saved repeat count for a resource token that crosses a descriptor or child boundary.
Relocated entry word $2E68 followed by a body length of $055A.
Clear the input latch, install the title interrupt vector from $31D9 and start the DP and GP modules with display IDs in X and Y.
Pass ID $C2/$30 to DS through $38-$39.
Pass ID $C2/$31 to DS through $38-$39.
Call DP with mode 1, set $33 to 8 and increment the pending display flag at $32. On the first visit, look up S1 and start its tune through $6400.
Immediate startup counter incremented at $3083. Its nonzero value on subsequent visits skips the first music setup.
